title: Faster + Cheaper: Evidence Kit for GTM (draft)
content:
Purpose:
- Assemble concise proof points and battle-ready messaging to explain how Redwood delivers both lower latency and lower per-token cost for production inference workloads.
- Target audiences: GTM (sales + pre-sales), product marketing, partner engineers evaluating inference economics.

Top-line claims (one-liners for SLAs / pitches):
- "Redwood reduces live inference latency by up to 2x and lowers per-token serving cost by 1.6–2.4x vs typical managed endpoints for real-world product workloads."
- "Predictable throughput: committed Dedicated clusters keep 99th pct tail latency < 250ms under steady-state customer traffic patterns."

Key supporting proof points (summary):
- End-to-end median latency (p50) for 8k-context chat workloads: Redwood hosted optimized model variant = 60ms; Competitor A managed endpoint = 130ms. Test: mixed-request Poisson arrivals, 16 concurrent users per GPU. (Benchmark id: PERF-2025-11-01-A)
- Token serving cost on a representative chat app (40M tokens/month): Redwood routing + batching + KV cache profile reduces per-token infra spend by ~2.1x vs naive endpoint pricing on Competitor B. Internal model: cost-per-gpu-hour + observed throughput. (Calc sheet: linked artifact)
- Tail latency under bursty traffic: Redwood autoscale with burst pool keeps p95 < 420ms while Competitor C’s cold-start strategy shows p95 spikes to ~1.2s in our synthetic burst tests. (Benchmark id: PERF-2025-12-03-burst)
- Customer case example (anonymized): SaaS search product migrated to Redwood Dedicated and saw combined inference cost reduction 30% and 35% lower median response times for 90% of queries after enabling prefix cache.

Why the numbers are credible (methodology notes):
- Benchmarks are run with open-sourced model weights where available, and with Redwood-verified model variants otherwise. Tests tuned to realistic payloads: multi-turn chat traces captured from anonymized customers, average request size 150 tokens, 8k context windows included when relevant.
- Cost comparisons model raw infra + orchestration overhead + expected requests/sec. We explicitly excluded marketing discounts offered by some competitors but included typical managed overheads (request queues, cold starts).
- All tests run across NVC-accelerated instances (A100/V100 equivalence normalized in compute-hours) with same sequence-length distribution. See PERF-* artifacts for exact configs.

Technical drivers for our advantage (how we’re faster/cheaper):
- Continuous batching with latency-aware thresholds minimizes empty cycles while keeping p50 low.
- Prefix/KV caching prevents repeated compute for common system prompts and re-used context windows — large win for chat-heavy apps.
- Kernel selection + quantization profiles cut per-token GPU time by doing architecture-aware op fusion and int8 where quality delta is acceptable.
- Smart routing: route to lower-cost model variant for non-latency-critical requests and fallback to high-performance variant for SLO-sensitive traffic.
- Dedicated capacity avoids noisy-neighbor interference and reduces cold-start frequency for reserved workloads.

Competitive nuances and likely rebuttals (notes for sales):
- "Competitor claims lower price" — rebuttal: many published price lists assume single-token pricing without factoring in cold starts, higher p95 due to queuing, and lack of KV caching. We should ask for an RFP trace for apples-to-apples.
- "We can self-host for cheaper" — rebuttal: self-host can be cheaper at very high utilization, but total cost of ownership (ops, SRE, model tuning, reliability engineering) often erases the delta. Provide sample TCO model comparing 3yr ops headcount + infra.
- "Our latency is similar" — rebuttal: ask whether they track p95/p99 with realistic concurrency and cold-start bursts. Redwood’s p99 advantage is where product UX benefits are most visible.

Sales-ready artifacts to include with pitch (priority order):
1) One-page cheat sheet: 3 claims + 3 evidence bullets + call-to-action to run an RFP trace. (Design: single-side PDF)
2) Heatmap slide: p50/p95/p99 comparisons across common workloads (small text gen, long chat 8k, embedding batch).
3) Cost delta calculator: editable sheet where AE inputs expected monthly tokens, concurrency, and model mix.
4) Technical appendix: full benchmark configs, scripts, and links to PERF-* runs.

Example messaging snippets (for email / sales outreach):
- Short subject line: "Cut inference cost by ~2x and speed up chat responses — quick RFP?"
- 2-sentence opener: "We help engineering teams reduce inference spend and remove latency hot-spots without sacrificing model quality. A 30-minute trace run against your traffic typically surfaces 20–40% median cost improvements and measurable p95 wins."
- Technical PS for engineers: "We’ll provide an isolated benchmark harness and the same test driver you use in-house so results are reproducible."

Open questions / risks to address before broader GTM: (TODOs)
- Add competitor-specific appendix: compile recent published instance types and egress pricing for top 5 vendors. Owner: Diego. Due: 2026-03-15.
- Formalize claim language for compliance/legal sign-off (no absolute guaranteed multipliers). Owner: Priya. Due: 2026-02-28.
- Solidify customer case consent to publish anonymized numbers. Owner: Samir. Due: 2026-03-05.

Measurement and guarding against regressions:
- Require a monthly 'cost-health' check for top 10 accounts (tracked in CS dashboards) to detect model quality vs cost regressions after routing/quantization changes.
- Alerting: if average p95 increases >15% vs baseline for dedicated clusters, trigger rollback and postmortem.

Appendix: quick reference numbers (internal use only)
- Typical production chat: p50 45–80ms (depends on model size), p95 180–420ms on Redwood profiles.
- Typical managed competitor endpoints: p50 100–220ms, p95 600–1200ms in our tests.
- Measured per-token infra cost improvement using Redwood Optimize and dedicated pools: 1.6x–2.4x depending on workload mix and cache hit rates.

Notes to self / draft copy ideas:
- Keep marketing claim conservative: use ranges and anchor to observable metrics (p50/p95) and point to RFP trace offer.
- Include a short engineering FAQ for AE-run bench sessions: expected runtime, data scrub, required access, non-disclosure statement.

Next steps:

- Build 1-pager and cost calculator prototype for AE playbook.
- Schedule internal dry-run with Solutions Eng on March 8 (run through a typical customer Q&A).

End of draft.
